pll2d14c8-d1e3520.summary: Asks where the waters were gathered, since they covered all space to heaven: the earth may have sunk to make hollows, or the first waters were thinner, like mist, and were condensed. 'One place' is said because all seas and rivers join the great sea; then 'gatherings' in the plural for its many bays (Bede).
claims: The gathering is explained by sinking earth or condensed waters.
All waters are continuous with the great sea.

pl-l2d14c8.summary: Asks where the gathered waters went, since they had covered all the space up to heaven: the earth may have sunk to provide hollows, or the first waters were thinner, like mist, and were condensed and easily gathered. Though there are many seas and rivers, Scripture says 'into one place' because all waters are continuous with the great sea, then 'gatherings' in the plural for its many bays (Bede).
claims: The earth may have sunk to receive the waters.
The first waters may have been thinner and condensed when gathered.
All waters are 'in one place' because all connect to the great sea.
